name: Spring onion
botanicalName: Allium fistulosum (also sold in SA as young-harvested Allium cepa)
harvestProduct: whole young plant (leaves and unswollen/lightly-swollen stem), sold in bunches
botanicalNameNotes: No dedicated SA government or KZN DARD document for spring/bunching onion was found in this research pass. KZN DARD's general 'Onion' chapter (for bulb onion, Allium cepa) notes: 'A small portion of the crop is sometimes harvested when the bulbs are sufficiently sized and are marketed as green onions, usually in bunches.' (kzndard.gov.za, Onion, p.4) — i.e. in SA commercial practice 'spring onion'/'green onion' is often just an early-pulled bulb-onion crop, not a separate botanical species. A Starke Ayres home-garden catalogue separately sells a distinct 'Broad-leaved spring onion... Perennial' product, consistent with true non-bulbing Allium fistulosum (Welsh onion). Both usages exist in the SA market; this file could not determine which one the source data actually describes for most fields, and treats the two as separate lines of evidence.
frostTenderNotes: Not addressed by any source found for this crop specifically.
transplantNotes: Not established. Bulb-onion-type spring onion would typically be direct-sown or transplanted like table onion (both practiced per KZN DARD's 'Onion' chapter); a true perennial bunching type (Allium fistulosum) is usually direct-sown or division-propagated. No source distinguishes practice for a 'spring onion' product specifically.

summer.notes: No primary source found. Left empty rather than substituting the general bulb-onion calendar (KZN 'Plant Establishment' Table 6: Onion — Cold areas Feb-Mar) for a distinct crop.

daysToHarvestRange.notes: No primary source found. A Starke Ayres home-garden catalogue gives 75-95 days for an unnamed 'Broad-leaved spring onion' and 90 days for 'Slender Star' — recorded here as context only, not as the sourced value, per the brief's rule that seed catalogues are not an acceptable sole source for a number (quote: 'DAYS TO MATURITY: 75-95' / 'DAYS TO MATURITY: 90', Starke Ayres Seed & Garden Care Catalogue, First Edition, p.24-25).

rowSpacingRangeCm.notes: No primary source found for spring onion specifically. KZN DARD's bulb-onion spacing (Rows 200-300mm, Plant 60-80mm — 'Plant Establishment' Table 5, p.5) is not substituted here since spring onion is typically grown at closer spacing than a bulb crop; recorded as a gap.

inRowSpacingRangeCm.notes: See rowSpacingRangeCm notes — no primary source found.

yield.notes: KZN DARD's 'Onion' chapter states 'Yields can vary from about 15 to over 40 tons per hectare' (p.4) for the bulb crop — not usable for a bunched, immature-harvest product sold by the bunch rather than by mass in the same way. No yield figure specific to spring/bunching onion was found. Recorded as a gap.

ecocropNotes: EcoCrop_DB.csv also has an 'Allium cepa' row (TOPMN 12, TOPMX 25, TMIN 4, TMAX 30, GMIN 85, GMAX 175) which would apply instead if the crop in practice is a young-harvested bulb onion rather than true Allium fistulosum. Both are recorded here; the Allium fistulosum row was chosen as primary since it is the closer botanical match to a true non-bulbing 'spring onion'.

varietiesNotes: Zones left null for both cultivars — the catalogue gives only a generic season claim, not SA regional recommendations, and no other source distinguishes these two products by growing region. The two cultivars' differing season claims (one year-round, one Autumn/Winter-only) were not reconciled into a single crop-level sowMonths calendar because they may represent genuinely different botanical products (see botanicalNameNotes).

gaps: No dedicated SA government, provincial or ARC production guideline for spring/bunching onion was located — this is the weakest-sourced crop in this batch.

Ambiguity over whether 'spring onion' in the SA smallholder/retail context means a distinct Allium fistulosum crop or an early-pulled Allium cepa (bulb onion) crop was not resolved by any source found; both are documented as existing.

sowMonths, daysToHarvestRange, row/in-row spacing, sow depth, seed rate and yield are all unsourced from a primary/official document; only two seed-catalogue variety listings (Starke Ayres) were found, which per the brief cannot be used as the sole source for these numeric fields.
No zone-specific information found for any of the 8 SA growing zones.
frostTender and transplant practice are both unconfirmed.
summary: No DAFF, ARC or KZN DARD production guideline dedicated to spring/bunching onion was found despite multiple targeted searches; KZN's general Onion chapter only notes in passing that bulb onion is sometimes pulled young and bunched as 'green onions'. The only concrete finds were two Starke Ayres home-garden seed-catalogue listings ('Slender Star' and an unnamed 'broad-leaved' perennial type) giving season and approximate days-to-maturity, which under the brief's sourcing rules cannot stand in for the core sourced numeric fields. All agronomic fields (sowMonths, spacing, yield, days-to-harvest) are recorded as gaps.
